title: MV I don't know how to scale sprite s properly or make them bigger for MV

posts.author: NS24
posts.body:
I'm so lost with trying to figure this out. I made a sprite sheet for a pixel character I made a good while ago, but when I try to put it in MV, it's pretty small, but I want it to be bigger.
I'm new to RPG Maker and I'm not too familiar when it comes to using grids in LibreSprite, but I don't know to make this work how I want it to work.

posts.author: Midona018
posts.body:
Could you add screenshots of your character sheet and how it looks in-game ? If it is 48 px tall it should be the same size as RTP characters, but if it's smaller you will have to resize it manually (or use  a plugin, but if you're new you should try without).
To resize a character sheet, the best is to make it manually in an editor (maybe use RTP sheets as a size reference) but you can also use websites like
waifu2x.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
depends but mostly no.
only full percentage resizes (x200%, x300%, x400% etc) can be made lossless, and even that requires you to know what you're doing and using a professional image program.
any other form of resize will always lose quality - that is almost a guarantee, and the reason why big companies like Adobe spent a lot of money for improving their resize algorithms.
The better the algorithm used, the better the results - but it will never be completely lossless.
You'll have to put in quite a lot of effort to find a better resizer. Is that worth the improvement compared to redoing the key characters?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
You don't need to redo the characters. As Andar just suggested, you simply need to use any photo editing app of your choice (Gimp is free), set the scale method to nearest neighbor, and resize it to either 200% or 300%.
(though I am not sure why he says "professional image program". I think nearly any photo editing program has scaling)
tbh, I have no idea why Midona used waifu2x. Waifu2x is an AI based upscaler primarily meant for upscaling anime. Not only is it an overkill solution for a very easy 200% upscale, pixel art isn't it's trained material and is likely why the output results looked funky.

Click to expand...
scaling yes, but a lot of them give no option for the choice of the algorithm used.
and an image program that scales only with "average colour" instead of "nearest neighbour" will not keep the quality as that algorithm was developed for photo resizing, not for pixel art.
